items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: And that brought me to music, Chet Baker’s singing brought me to music.

ctx.x: Oh, I adore him. Because he sang like he played. I totally adored him. My father was a professor so whenever we came home early from school, my brother Klaus and me — Klaus played drums in my room and I sang. And we had a Chet Baker record going. And I just loved the softness of his voice. He loved the way he phrased. I loved the songs that he sang, [sings] “Time After Time” [scats]. The warmth of his voice, very relaxed, and the way he phrased. Chet Baker couldn’t sit and read one note. Chet Baker couldn’t read…

such a cool guy you know, that he quit. It was just the way he played. He must have been also, when he wasn’t on drugs, a great guy. I heard him say on some weird tape, some announcements to the audience you know, “You’d better listen.” You know, talk about listening, very intelligent, very beautiful. But the drugs killed him. And that brought me to music, Chet Baker’s singing brought me to music. So I always wanted to be a dancer, and my parents sometimes had the money, sometimes didn’t have it. And dance you…
Yeah. I always feel sorry for dancers too because by the time you’re 30, you’re like — then you’re going to have to become a teacher you know.
